engagement_background.objective: Deliver measurable procurement cost savings and leverage APDerm’s enterprise-wide buying power to support Waud Capital’s value-creation goals amid inflationary, pandemic-impacted market conditions.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Two-phase strategic sourcing program covering more than 10 indirect spend categories with a combined addressable baseline of approximately $6.3 million. Phase 1 tackled high-priority areas such as medical supplies, courier, small parcel, telecom, IT hardware and office supplies; Phase 2 focused on billing services, janitorial, IT managed services, laundry/linen, non-IT temporary labor, copier/print services and uniforms, while recently re-contracted waste management was excluded.
constraints_challenges: Decentralized purchasing across dozens of acquired clinic locations created a fragmented supplier base.
Limited spend visibility and inconsistent vendor usage data; significant effort required to cleanse AP data and obtain contracts.
Inflationary environment and supply-chain disruptions during COVID-19 complicated price negotiations.
Long-standing incumbent relationships made supplier change sensitive, requiring a ‘soft-touch’ negotiation approach.
Compressed timeline driven by private-equity value-creation expectations and need for rapid savings realization.
Limited internal resources available to manage vendor transitions and provide timely stakeholder input.

procurement_environment.data_availability: AP invoice data for 10/1/20-9/30/21 extracted from accounting system; ad-hoc contract files gathered on request; no centralized contract repository.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Multiple duplicate vendor names, unmapped GL codes, and gaps where suppliers did not provide historical usage detail, requiring manual cleanup before analysis.

extraction_sources: Agreement/Procurement Cost Reduction Services Agreement_APDerm_12.11.20 - signed.pdf
extraction_notes: Operating model explicitly described as 'decentralized' in case study.
Maturity assessed as low based on fragmented supply base, lack of leveraged contracts and need for Treya to run full sourcing process.
Data availability and quality inferred from AP spend files and agreement data-collection clause; confidence medium because internal systems detail not fully documented.
